title: Welcome - how this repository is organised
body:
Hi! This is our space for the Virtual Tone Microphone project.

**Quick tour**
- **Issues + Project board**: all the work, split into milestones M0-M4. Each milestone has an epic that tracks its issues.
- **Discussions**: Decisions (RFCs), Q&A, Meeting notes, Status updates.
- **docs/**: setup guide, architecture, requirements traceability, testing, ADRs, glossary.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: how we use branches, PRs, labels, and our Definition of Done.

**First steps for everyone**
1. Go through docs/setup.md and tick your name in the setup issue.
2. Have a look at the Kickoff discussion and the open RFCs.

Nothing here is set in stone. If something about the structure doesn't work for you, say so and we'll change it.

title: Kickoff: areas, availability and the first milestone
body:
To get started, it would help to agree on a few things together:

1. **Areas**: the project splits fairly naturally into three parts. One possible split:
   - Driver core (endpoint, stream, timer DPC, generator, synchronization)
   - Interface & integration (control channel, IOCTL handlers, library, install/uninstall, Driver Verifier)
   - GUI & tests (GUI, gtest, later presets and monitoring)

   Which part would you prefer? Everyone can still work anywhere; this is mainly about who keeps an eye on what.
2. **Availability**: when are you usually available, and are there any busy periods coming up?
3. **First milestone**: M0 is about getting everyone's environment working and making the main decisions. Does that sound like the right first step?
4. **Sync**: would a short weekly call work for everyone, and which day?

Please reply with your thoughts. I'll update docs/team.md once we agree.

title: RFC: Driver model - PortCls vs ACX
body:
### Context
Spec item 9 allows PortCls (WDM) or ACX (KMDF). Spec item 2 requires Windows 10 **and** 11.

### Options
**PortCls**: mature, both reference samples use it, lots of documentation. More boilerplate.

**ACX**: newer and simpler on paper, built on KMDF. Fewer samples, and Windows 10 support needs to be confirmed.

### Open question
Is ACX available on Windows 10? If not, PortCls is the only option that meets the spec.

The result goes into docs/adr/0001-driver-model.md.

title: RFC: Base sample - SimpleAudioSample vs SysVAD
body:
### Context
Starting from a working Microsoft sample saves a lot of time.

### Options
**SimpleAudioSample**: small, easy to strip down to one capture endpoint.

**SysVAD**: already has a virtual device with simulated capture from a generated tone, but it's very large.

**Hybrid**: start from SimpleAudioSample and borrow tone generation / capture timing from SysVAD.

What did you find when looking at them? The result goes into docs/adr/0002-base-sample.md.

title: RFC: How the GUI reaches the driver
body:
### Context
The GUI talks to the driver through a library that wraps IOCTLs (spec item 6). In a PortCls driver, PortCls owns the dispatch routines, so our IOCTLs need a deliberate path.

### Options
- **A.** Device interface on the audio device + our own IRP_MJ_DEVICE_CONTROL handling, forwarding everything else to PortCls.
- **B.** Separate control device object.
- **C.** Custom KS property (more audio-native, but the spec asks for IOCTLs).

Details and pros/cons are in docs/adr/0003-control-channel.md. Depends on the driver model decision.

title: RFC: Shared interface (VirtualToneIoctl.h)
body:
### Context
common/VirtualToneIoctl.h is shared by the driver and the library. Agreeing on it early lets the driver, library and GUI be built in parallel.

### Draft
- 3 IOCTLs: get params, set params, get version
- One struct: Version, Enabled, Waveform, FrequencyHz, AmplitudePercent
- Limits and defaults from the spec, plus a shared validation macro

Synchronization proposal (docs/adr/0004-parameter-synchronization.md): spin lock around the struct, the DPC copies it to a local snapshot.

Please review the header and comment on anything you'd change.

title: RFC: GUI framework - Qt vs C#
body:
### Context
The spec allows any framework. The library is native code, so the choice affects how the GUI calls it.

### Options
**Qt (C++)**: calls the library directly; heavier toolchain.

**C# (WPF/WinForms)**: fast UI development; needs P/Invoke to the library.

Main factor: what the person mainly working on the GUI prefers. Result goes into docs/adr/0005-gui-framework.md.

title: Environment setup problems - post them here
body:
Stuck on Visual Studio, the WDK, test signing, the VM or installing the sample? Post the symptom and what you tried.

When it's solved, mark the answer and add a line to the Gotchas section of docs/setup.md.
